items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: You haven't mentioned some of the women who are supposed to have made contributions, like Ma Rainey... Were they sort of on the outside of what you people did, or what?

ctx.x: No, I just beat my wife in the... They couldn't go, no, minors couldn't go in the barroom. No, man. They couldn't go, man. They couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. That's right. You can't be in the ballroom. And at that time, when they couldn't go in the ballroom, they had so many parties and dancers here, go over there. They didn't go in there. They didn't go in there. Why? Because you cannot go in the ballroom. They have to go there. Now,…

Talk about ruling. That's where they rule you at. Yeah, that's where it is. Incidentally, during your conversation, you've all talked about the boys with whom you've played, and the boys with whom you've brought out. Oh, excuse me. And you haven't mentioned some of the women who are supposed to have made contributions, like Ma Rainey, Bessie Smith, and so on. Were they sort of on the outside of what you people did, or what? With Ma Rainey then? Yeah, those two. Or others. Yeah, quite a few others. Yeah. But no.
